title: X-band near-perfect absorber based on electromagnetic metasurface
content:
by Changliang Lin, Hanhui Wang, Kaitong Wang, Xiong Wang, Gongnan Li

The development of compact, miniaturized absorbers in the microwave band is of great significance for enhancing the performance of small aerial platforms such as unmanned aerial vehicles. Conventional absorbers typically rely on materials with specific thicknesses or on active components, which limits their applicability in practical scenarios. To address these issues, this work proposes a metasurface-based approach in which dipole resonances are engineered to achieve impedance matching, realizing a maximum absorptance of 99.6% at 10 GHz for optimized device. At the same time, the absorber maintains an absorptance above 50% for incidence angles ranging from 0° to 70°. Finite-element simulations are employed to elucidate the physical origin of the absorption and the impact of varying structural parameters. The proposed absorber features a simple architecture with a thickness of only one-thirtieth of the operating wavelength, while offering a very high degree of design freedom, thereby providing a feasible route toward practical, miniaturized microwave devices.
author: Changliang Lin
